Subject: Renewal: proposal to expand reserved pool and migrate A100 → H100/L40S (performance-per-dollar brief)

Hi Julia —

Quick note ahead of your Nov 30 renewal: thank you again for the partnership this year. Based on usage trends from the past 12 months we see two clear opportunities to lower your per-token cost and improve tail latency for your inference workloads:

- Add 20% reserved capacity to your Dedicated pool to remove bursting risk for peak inference windows.
- Regrade the pool from A100 to H100 (primary) with L40S as a fallback model family for lower-memory workloads.

I want to share a short performance-per-dollar (PPD) brief and a proposal that shows total cost of ownership over the next 12 months with and without the regrade. Can we block 30 minutes this week to walk through the numbers + procurement steps? I’ve CC’d Lauren (solutions) to help with the rollout plan.

Attachments: draft proposal + perf brief (I’ll follow up with the detailed CSV after your reply).

Proposed times (PST): Tue 11/9 10:00–10:30, Wed 11/10 09:00–09:30. Which works for you?

Best,
Monica

Subject: Re: Renewal: proposal to expand reserved pool and migrate A100 → H100/L40S (performance-per-dollar brief)

Julia / Ken / procurement team —

Thanks — attached is the detailed brief and the CSV with measured throughput samples from your most common model families (last 60 days). Highlights up front:

High-level PPD and performance summary (representative):
- Current baseline (A100, fp16): 1.0x PPD (baseline), median throughput 1,000 tokens/sec, 95th latency = 240ms, $0.000012 / token (effective, after committed discounts).
- H100 (tf32 + flash-attn path, quantized INT8 on trimmed models): 1.45x PPD vs A100, median throughput 1,450 tokens/sec (+45%), 95th latency = 160ms (-33%), projected $0.000010 / token (after migration and commit).
- L40S (sparse-friendly, lower-memory): 1.15x PPD for the LLMs that fit within L40S memory profile, median throughput 1,150 tokens/sec, 95th latency = 180ms.

Why the regrade helps (short):
- Kernel-level improvements for large-context attention and better memory bandwidth on H100 yield ~30–50% throughput gains for your peak seq-lengths (we validated on your 8–12k prompts).
- Quantization tooling in Redwood Optimize gives ~15–20% lower cost on H100 without material quality loss for your common prompts.
- L40S provides a lower-cost path for shorter-context, high-QPS calls and reduces the pressure on H100 memory for big-batch runs.

Proposed commercial options (12-month view):
1) Conservative: +20% reserved GPUs, keep A100 primary, add L40S for 10% of workload — ~+6% monthly spend, immediate SLA uplift with throughput cushion.
2) Balanced (recommended): migrate 60% of pool to H100, 20% to L40S, +20% reserved capacity — ~+12% monthly spend but 40% net reduction in $/inference when accounting for improved PPD and reduced retry/burst costs.
3) Aggressive: full pool regrade to H100 with +25% reserve and a 3-month canary (we can rollback per route) — ~+20% monthly spend but target 50% reduction in peak per-token cost after quantization and operational optimizations.

Rollout and guarantees:
- Canary plan: staged route-by-route migration (60% → 80% → 100%) with automated fallback to A100 pool for any route exceeding latency SLOs.
- Throughput guarantees: we can include a dedicated throughput SLA for peak-hour windows (example: sustained 1,200 tokens/sec per reserved GPU with 99th percentile latency guard) as a short-term addendum to the renewal.

Next steps if you want to proceed:
- I’ll send an updated commitment amendment + SOW with the chosen option (1/2/3) and exact seat counts.
- Procurement: Ben will include standard order forms and DocuSign link.
- Technical onboarding: Lauren will prepare the migration playbook and run a canary in your staging region.

Attachments included: perf-comparison-A100-H100-L40S.csv (detailed run outputs), 20271107-acme-proposal.pdf (commercial options), ppd-scenario-breakdown.xlsx (assumptions).

We’ll hold the Wed 11/10 09:00 PST meeting — calendar invite to follow.

Thanks,
Monica
